stable_traits.personality: Commanding, protective, vigilant. Pledged to fight the Dark One from birth.

characters.notes: Warder bond with Moiraine evident (she would know the moment of his death). His role as protector and scout is prominent.

stable_traits.personality: Calm, authoritative, knowledgeable, strategic. Demonstrates patience and control even under stress.

characters.notes: Uses the One Power to set wards. Has warder bond with Lan.

stable_traits.filiations: Son of Tam al'Thor (or believes so, with doubts emerging)
stable_traits.personality: Thoughtful, cautious. Shows growing anxiety about his parentage.

characters.notes: Internal doubt about parentage expressed: 'Some of us can't even be sure of that' regarding fathers. Carries Tam's sword.

stable_traits.personality: Impulsive, treasure-hungry, reckless. Troubled by the Old Blood speaking through him.

characters.notes: Still processing the incident where he spoke Aemon's warcry in the Old Tongue. Drawn to treasure despite danger.

stable_traits.personality: Cautious, thoughtful. More inclined to follow rules and ask permission than Mat.

characters.notes: Carries an axe. Shows careful temperament, wanting to ask Moiraine before exploring.

stable_traits.age: Old enough to move stiffly and need to knuckle his back
stable_traits.personality: Knowledgeable about lore and history. Wry and somewhat cynical. Warns against dangerous talk of rebirth.

characters.notes: Provides exposition about the Old Blood and warns about discussing rebirth. Smokes a long-stemmed pipe.

stable_traits.personality: Sharp-tongued, protective, stubborn. Skilled with herbs. Shows tension with Lan but commitment to helping those in need.

aliases_observed.notes: Her role in the Women's Circle

characters.notes: Provided herbs to help Moiraine recover. Bristles at the boys' recklessness.
Present but relatively passive in this chapter. Shows fear at the story and the boys' return.

stable_traits.physical_traits: Sleek, overfed, completely bald, drooping eyelids. Wears tight black breeches, soft red boots, long red vest embroidered in gold, white shirt with wide sleeves. No shadow.
stable_traits.age: Ancient—existed during the Trolloc Wars, centuries ago
stable_traits.filiations: Was adviser to King Balwen Mayel of Aridhol
stable_traits.personality: Malevolent, deceptive, parasitic. Seeks to consume souls and escape Shadar Logoth by possessing someone.

characters.notes: Not truly human anymore—a spiritual entity trapped in Shadar Logoth. Can change size and form, vanish into cracks like smoke. Gave Aridhol the battlecry 'The victory of the Light is all' while leading them to abandon the Light. Survived the destruction of Aridhol but is bound to the city. Seeks to possess someone to escape.

stable_traits.physical_traits: Became a withered shell with the light of madness in his eyes
stable_traits.filiations: King of Aridhol during the Trolloc Wars
stable_traits.personality: Corrupted by Mordeth. Descended into madness.

characters.notes: Historical figure. King of Aridhol who was corrupted by Mordeth's counsel.

stable_traits.filiations: Son of Thorin al'Toren al Ban (King of Manetheren)

aliases_observed.notes: His title as prince of Manetheren

characters.notes: Historical figure. Tried to win Aridhol back to the Second Covenant. Escaped Aridhol's dungeons and fled to the Borderlands where he met and married Rhea, leading to tragedy.

stable_traits.filiations: Married Prince Caar without knowing who he was

characters.notes: Historical figure. Killed Caar (her husband) and then herself. Her actions led to the fall of Aleth-Loriel.

stable_traits.filiations: Father of Caar. King of Manetheren.

characters.notes: Historical figure. King of Manetheren during the time Balwen Mayel was King of Aridhol.

Moiraine's horse. Thom takes her reins.

stable_traits.personality: Watches people but gives Perrin no trouble

stable_traits.filiations: Father of Rand (or believed to be)

characters.notes: Not physically present. Mentioned only as the owner of the sword Rand carries and in Rand's dream.
Historical figure. Mentioned in context of Mat speaking his warcry in the Old Tongue in a previous chapter.

appearances.whereabouts: Leading the group into Shadar Logoth, then leaving to scout for Trollocs, returning at night with news
appearances.notable_actions: Leads group into the ruined city. Commands the boys to bring horses inside and stable them. Goes out to scout. Returns with Trolloc badges, reports over 100 Trollocs and 4 Myrddraal heading toward them. Demonstrates his warder bond connection to Moiraine.
appearances.demeanor: Commanding, protective, efficient. Shows concern when Moiraine mentions the wards.

appearances.whereabouts: In the ruined building in Shadar Logoth, recovering from exhaustion
appearances.notable_actions: Initially being carried by Lan. Sets wards around the building to protect from Mashadar and other evils of Shadar Logoth. Questions the boys intensely about Mordeth. Tells the history of Aridhol/Shadar Logoth and Mordeth. Plans their escape by river. Rises quickly when Lan returns despite her earlier exhaustion.
appearances.demeanor: Calm, authoritative, knowledgeable. Shows brief alarm about Mordeth but quickly regains composure. Demonstrates deep historical knowledge.

appearances.whereabouts: Exploring Shadar Logoth with Mat and Perrin, then returning to the group's shelter
appearances.notable_actions: Explores the ruined city. Encounters Mordeth. Notices Mordeth has no shadow. Escapes from Mordeth's attack. Feels watched by unseen eyes throughout the city. Has troubled sleep with nightmares. Wakes and adds wood to the fire. Internal doubts about his parentage surface.
appearances.demeanor: Awestruck by the city initially, then increasingly frightened. Cautious and watchful. Troubled by thoughts of his father.

appearances.whereabouts: Exploring Shadar Logoth with Rand and Perrin
appearances.notable_actions: Enthusiastically explores the city. Discovers Mordeth and the treasure room. Extremely eager about the treasure, reluctant to leave it. Reveals to Mordeth that they're traveling to Tar Valon. Barely escapes Mordeth's attack. Still troubled by speaking in the Old Tongue earlier.
appearances.demeanor: Excited, reckless, treasure-obsessed. Shows glum introspection when thinking about the Old Blood incident. Defensive when blamed for the trouble.

appearances.whereabouts: Exploring Shadar Logoth with Rand and Mat
appearances.notable_actions: Explores the city. Picks up a jeweled axe from treasure but sets it back down. More cautious than Mat, wanting to ask Moiraine before exploring. Helps drag Mat away from the treasure. Unsaddles Mandarb without trouble from the fierce stallion.
appearances.demeanor: Cautious, thoughtful, rule-following. Shows fear but maintains reason.

appearances.whereabouts: In the ruined building, tending the fire
appearances.notable_actions: Unsaddles horses. Smokes his pipe. Provides crucial exposition about the Old Blood and warns against talking of rebirth and dead men taking living bodies. Mutters 'fools' when the boys return.
appearances.demeanor: Wry, knowledgeable, somewhat exasperated with the boys' recklessness. Cautious about dangerous topics.

appearances.whereabouts: In the ruined building, tending to Moiraine
appearances.notable_actions: Provides herbs to help Moiraine recover. Berates the boys for running off. Has tense exchange with Lan about her herbs and his sword. Shows concern when Lan is gone long.
appearances.demeanor: Sharp-tongued, angry at the boys, protective. Defensive of her healing skills against Lan's skepticism.

appearances.whereabouts: In the ruined building by the fire
appearances.notable_actions: Helps Nynaeve by holding her herb bag. Startled when the boys return. Asks if the Dark One is outside when the Myrddraal are mentioned.
appearances.demeanor: Frightened, concerned. Relatively passive in this chapter.

appearances.whereabouts: In the ruined city of Shadar Logoth, in a large building with columns and underground treasure rooms
appearances.notable_actions: Appears among columns, claims to be a treasure hunter. Leads the boys down to an underground treasure room. Attempts to trick them into helping carry treasure outside the city (which would allow him to possess one of them). Becomes enraged when he learns they're going to Tar Valon. Transforms into a huge monstrous form trying to grab them. Shrinks back after the boys scream. Dives across the room and vanishes into a crack in the wall like smoke, shouting 'You are all dead!'
appearances.demeanor: Initially smooth and accommodating. Becomes violently enraged and fearful when Tar Valon is mentioned. Demonstrates supernatural abilities and malevolence.

appearances.whereabouts: Historical—ruled Aridhol during the Trolloc Wars
appearances.notable_actions: Was corrupted by Mordeth. Ordered the deaths of Prince Caar and his embassy. Descended into madness.

appearances.whereabouts: Historical—traveled from Manetheren to Aridhol and then fled to the Borderlands
appearances.notable_actions: Tried to win Aridhol back to the Second Covenant. Was imprisoned in Aridhol's dungeons. Escaped and fled to Borderlands with Mordeth's assassins pursuing him. Married Rhea. His actions set in motion events leading to his death at Rhea's hands and the fall of Aleth-Loriel.

appearances.whereabouts: Historical—in the Borderlands where she met Caar
appearances.notable_actions: Married Prince Caar without knowing his identity. Killed him. Killed herself before his tomb.
Ruled as King of Manetheren when Balwen Mayel was King of Aridhol. Father of Caar.

appearances.whereabouts: In the ruined building being used as shelter
appearances.notable_actions: Brought inside and unsaddled by Rand.

appearances.notable_actions: Brought inside and unsaddled by Rand.

appearances.whereabouts: In the ruined building being used as shelter
appearances.notable_actions: Brought inside and unsaddled by Thom.

appearances.whereabouts: In the ruined building being used as shelter
appearances.notable_actions: Unsaddled by Perrin. Watches Perrin but gives him no trouble despite being fierce-eyed.

appearances.whereabouts: Not physically present (back in Two Rivers or unknown)
appearances.notable_actions: Appears only in Rand's dream as a boy carrying his sword.
Discussed in context of Mat having spoken his warcry.

relationships.description: Moiraine holds the warder bond with Lan. Each would know the moment and manner of the other's death.
Tension and conflict over healing methods and authority. Nynaeve is defensive about her herbs; Lan is skeptical.
Nynaeve states she doesn't like Moiraine but will help anyone who needs it. Professional healer relationship with underlying tension.
Son and father relationship, though Rand is developing doubts about whether Tam is truly his biological father.
Close friends from Emond's Field who explore together and watch out for each other.
Close friends from Emond's Field who explore together and watch out for each other.
Friends from Emond's Field, though Perrin is more cautious than Mat.
Mordeth was adviser to King Balwen and corrupted him, whispered poison in his ear, leading Aridhol to darkness.
Father and son. Thorin was King of Manetheren; Caar was his son and prince.
Married couple. Rhea did not know Caar's true identity when they married. She ultimately killed him and then herself.
Lan is Mandarb's rider and owner.
Moiraine is Aldieb's rider and owner.
